rows.title: Passive subdomain enumeration
rows.objective: Amass, Subfinder, crt.sh — discover subdomains without active probing

rows.title: Active subdomain / vhost fuzzing
rows.objective: FFUF/Gobuster vhost mode — find non-public subdomains and virtual hosts

rows.title: Technology stack fingerprinting
rows.objective: Wappalyzer, WhatWeb, response headers — identify frameworks, servers, CDN

rows.title: JavaScript source, source map, and endpoint analysis
rows.objective: Check JS bundles and source maps for exposed source, hardcoded keys, internal endpoint references, URLs, API routes, hidden paths, and parameterized endpoints. Use static extraction plus crawling to correlate JS-linked endpoints with reachable attack surface.

rows.title: Cloud storage & exposed bucket discovery
rows.objective: Search for exposed S3/GCS/Azure buckets via naming patterns — data leakage risk

rows.title: Subdomain takeover check
rows.objective: Check dangling CNAME records pointing to deprovisioned cloud services (S3, GitHub Pages, Heroku)

rows.title: HTTP security headers review
rows.objective: Missing HSTS, CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Permissions-Policy

rows.title: TLS/SSL configuration
rows.objective: Weak ciphers, TLS 1.0/1.1 support, self-signed cert, expired cert — testssl.sh

rows.title: HTTP methods enumeration
rows.objective: Test OPTIONS, TRACE, PUT, DELETE and verb-tunneling headers (X-HTTP-Method-Override, X-Method-Override) — identify dangerous methods enabled or override acceptance that changes POST into PUT/PATCH/DELETE

rows.title: Default / backup file discovery
rows.objective: Ffuf wordlist — .bak, .old, .swp, .git/, .env, DS_Store. Tech-specific: phpinfo.php, web.config, .htaccess, WEB-INF/web.xml, /actuator, /debug, server-status.

rows.title: HTTP Strict Transport Security review
rows.objective: Verify HSTS is present, correctly scoped, long-lived enough for the engagement context, and compatible with preload expectations where applicable.

rows.title: CORS misconfiguration
rows.objective: Origin reflection: send arbitrary Origin header — if reflected with ACAO+ACAC, credentials exposed. Test null origin, subdomain wildcard, pre-domain match (evildomain.target.com).

rows.title: HTTP Request Smuggling / desync testing
rows.objective: Test CL.TE, TE.CL, H2.CL, and H2.TE desync behavior to identify cache poisoning, front-end auth bypass, request queue poisoning, or delivered XSS through parser disagreement.

rows.title: SQL injection
rows.objective: Error-based, blind time-based (SLEEP/WAITFOR), Boolean, OOB. Tools: sqlmap -u URL --level=5 --risk=3. Test all input types including cookies/headers/JSON keys.

rows.title: NoSQL injection
rows.objective: MongoDB operator injection ($where, $gt) in JSON bodies

rows.title: Cross-Site Scripting (reflected, stored, and DOM)
rows.objective: Test reflected, stored, and DOM-based XSS across user-controlled inputs, URL fragments, client-side data flows, and rendered persisted content. Include encoding, context, and sanitizer bypass checks inside the parent XSS test rather than as standalone bypass rows.

rows.title: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI)
rows.objective: Identify engine from error (Jinja2, Twig, Freemarker, Pebble). Probe: {{7*7}}, ${7*7}, #{7*7}. Escalate to RCE via class loader or exec. Check user-controlled email/report templates.

rows.title: Command injection
rows.objective: OS injection in filename, conversion params, ping fields. Payloads: ; id, | id, $(id). Blind: time-based (sleep 5) or OOB DNS callback (curl attacker.com).

rows.title: HTTP Header injection / CRLF
rows.objective: Inject CRLF sequences to split responses, set cookies, redirect

rows.title: XXE injection
rows.objective: External entity injection in XML input — file read, SSRF, blind OOB

rows.title: BOLA — broken object level authorization
rows.objective: Manipulate object IDs in API paths/params to access other users' resources

rows.title: Mass assignment / excessive data exposure
rows.objective: POST/PUT with extra fields — check if they're written; check response for over-exposed fields

rows.title: Improper inventory — hidden API versions
rows.objective: Try /v1/, /v2/, /api/v0/, /internal/, /admin/ — older versions often lack new auth controls

rows.title: API security misconfiguration
rows.objective: Swagger/OpenAPI portal exposed, debug mode, stack traces, default credentials on API gateway

rows.title: Unrestricted resource consumption
rows.objective: No rate limiting on expensive API operations — batch requests, large payloads

rows.title: Web cache deception / poisoning
rows.objective: Path confusion (app.com/account/style.css), unkeyed header poisoning (X-Forwarded-Host)

rows.title: Known vulnerability scan
rows.objective: Nuclei, Nikto — check CVEs for identified web server, framework versions

rows.title: HTML injection
rows.objective: Inject HTML tags/attributes in reflected and stored contexts — verify untrusted markup cannot alter UI, links, email/report content, or phishing surfaces even when script execution is blocked

rows.title: Directory, content, robots, sitemap, and well-known discovery
rows.objective: Fuzz directories and content recursively, review robots.txt, sitemap.xml, and /.well-known/ paths, and enumerate hidden/admin/debug/API paths. Include tech extensions where relevant: PHP .php/.inc/.phtml, ASP.NET .asp/.aspx/.config, Java .jsp/.do/.action, Node .js/.json.

rows.title: Insecure deserialization
rows.objective: Java: ysoserial payloads via Burp Deserialization Scanner; magic bytes AC ED 00 05. PHP: unserialize() with POP chain via __wakeup/__destruct. Python: pickle.loads() RCE. .NET: BinaryFormatter, ViewState without MAC key (ysoserial.net).

rows.title: HTTP Parameter Pollution (HPP)
rows.objective: Duplicate params with different values: ?id=1&id=2, array notation id[]=1. PHP uses last value; ASP.NET joins with comma. Target: access control bypass, WAF evasion, OAuth redirect_uri manipulation.

rows.title: Prototype pollution
rows.objective: Inject __proto__[polluted]=1 or constructor[prototype][polluted]=1 in JSON body, query params, URL fragments. Use Burp DOM Invader for client-side sinks. Server-side: Node.js lodash/merge vulnerable patterns can lead to RCE.

rows.title: Exposed debug & admin endpoints
rows.objective: Probe /debug, /console, /admin, /actuator/*, /management, /.git/HEAD, /phpinfo.php, /server-status. Java/Spring: /actuator/heapdump, /actuator/env (may expose secrets). Tomcat: /manager/html, /host-manager.

rows.title: HTTP/2 specific testing
rows.objective: h2c upgrade smuggling: send Connection: Upgrade, Upgrade: h2c to backend. HTTP/2 request splitting via null bytes in headers. Test H2.CL / H2.TE desync with h2csmuggler. Verify HTTP/2 header injection with newlines.

rows.title: PHP-specific attack surface
rows.objective: phpinfo.php discloses full config and paths. LFI wrappers: php://filter/read=convert.base64-encode, php://input, data://text/plain;base64,. Type juggling: 0e magic hash bypass for loose == comparison. Check allow_url_include, auto_prepend_file.

rows.title: ASP.NET-specific attack surface
rows.objective: web.config via path traversal or IIS tilde shortname (8.3 filename ~). ViewState tampering if MAC key absent — ysoserial.net TypeConfuseDelegate. Trace.axd, elmah.axd exposure. ASPXAUTH cookie forging if machineKey leaked.

rows.title: Java / Tomcat-specific attack surface
rows.objective: Tomcat Manager (/manager/html, /manager/text) default creds (tomcat:tomcat, admin:admin) — WAR deploy for RCE. CVEs: CVE-2017-12617 PUT JSP upload, CVE-2020-1938 AJP Ghostcat. Spring Boot: /actuator/heapdump, /actuator/env. WEB-INF/web.xml disclosure.

rows.title: Node.js-specific attack surface
rows.objective: Prototype pollution via lodash/merge (< 4.17.11). Debug port exposure (--inspect 0.0.0.0:9229) -> RCE via DevTools protocol. ReDoS via user-supplied input to RegExp. npm audit for known CVEs. Dynamic require() path traversal in user-controlled input.

rows.title: Default credentials test
rows.objective: Try admin/admin, vendor defaults on login panels, admin paths

rows.title: Username enumeration
rows.objective: Compare response timing, size, message for valid vs invalid usernames

rows.title: Brute force & rate limit
rows.objective: Ffuf/Hydra on login & password-reset; verify lockout threshold, CAPTCHA, rate limiting. Bypass: X-Forwarded-For rotation, IP spoofing headers, credential stuffing with slow timing.

rows.title: JWT security testing
rows.objective: alg:none, RS256→HS256 confusion, weak secret brute force (hashcat), JWK injection, kid path traversal, expired token acceptance

rows.title: MFA / OTP bypass
rows.objective: Response manipulation, code reuse, OTP brute force (6-digit = 1M combinations), backup code abuse. Bypass: remove MFA step from response, replay same OTP across accounts.

rows.title: Password reset token security
rows.objective: Predictable tokens, token reuse, host header injection in reset email link

rows.title: Session token analysis
rows.objective: Check entropy, predictability, length of session tokens

rows.title: Cookie attribute review
rows.objective: Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict/Lax, Domain/Path scope

rows.title: Session fixation
rows.objective: Pre-auth session token reuse post-login — force victim to use known token

rows.title: CSRF testing
rows.objective: Missing/bypassable CSRF token, SameSite=None misuse, referer bypass

rows.title: Session invalidation on logout
rows.objective: Confirm server-side session destruction, token blacklisting on logout

rows.title: Session timeout enforcement
rows.objective: Idle timeout, absolute timeout — verify server enforces, not just client

rows.title: Forced browsing / direct object reference
rows.objective: Access restricted pages/objects without proper authorization (IDOR)

rows.title: Horizontal privilege escalation
rows.objective: Access resources belonging to peer-level users by manipulating IDs

rows.title: Vertical privilege escalation
rows.objective: Access admin/higher-privilege functions as a low-privilege user

rows.title: Path traversal
rows.objective: Test ../../etc/passwd in file params; encoded variants: %2F, ..%2F, %252F, ..;/. Null byte %00 to truncate extensions. PHP: php://filter, file:// wrappers.

rows.title: Broken Function Level Authorization (BFLA)
rows.objective: Access admin-level API endpoints as regular user by direct call

rows.title: Basic SSRF
rows.objective: URL params pointing to internal services, cloud metadata (169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data, 100.100.100.200 Alibaba). Test internal port scan via response time/error differences.

rows.title: SSRF bypass variants
rows.objective: Filter bypass: IPv6 [::1], decimal IP (2130706433), URL-encoded dots, DNS rebinding, redirect chains (open redirect -> internal), parser confusion with @, #, backslash.

rows.title: Protocol smuggling via SSRF
rows.objective: dict://, gopher:// to reach Redis, memcached, SMTP internally

rows.title: Web shell upload bypass
rows.objective: MIME bypass: change Content-Type to image/jpeg; double ext (.php.jpg); null byte (shell.php%00.jpg); magic bytes prepend. Check server-side execution path and storage location.

rows.title: Malicious file type upload
rows.objective: SVG XSS, HTML SSRF, polyglot files — check server-side validation depth

rows.title: Path traversal in download
rows.objective: Filename/path param to ../../etc/passwd; zip slip (../evil.jsp inside archive); encoded traversal. LFI wrappers: php://filter/convert.base64-encode/resource=index.php.

rows.title: Race conditions
rows.objective: Concurrent requests on limit-once operations — coupon use, refund, account creation

rows.title: Negative / zero value inputs
rows.objective: Negative price, zero quantity in payment/transaction flows

rows.title: Workflow / step bypass
rows.objective: Skip payment step, confirmation step — manipulate sequence via direct requests

rows.title: Unsafe third-party API consumption
rows.objective: Does app blindly trust 3rd-party API data without validation? SSRF via webhook URL

rows.title: LLM / AI prompt injection
rows.objective: User-controlled input passed to AI features — inject instructions to alter AI behavior or exfil data

rows.title: Blind SSRF
rows.objective: OOB detection via Burp Collaborator or interactsh. Inject in URL params, Referer, Host, X-Forwarded-For, PDF/image generation inputs, webhook fields. Confirm with DNS callback even if no HTTP response body.

rows.title: Email verification bypass
rows.objective: Access authenticated endpoints before verifying email. Test: change email to victim after verifying original, reuse token across accounts, IDOR on verify endpoint (/verify?token=X&user=Y), skip verification step via response manipulation.

rows.title: Password policy enforcement
rows.objective: Test min length (try 1-char), complexity bypass, common passwords (check Pwned Passwords). Verify server-side enforcement not just client-side JS. Test change/reset flows separately — policy often inconsistently applied.

rows.title: Injection in login fields
rows.objective: SQLi, NoSQLi in username/password fields — error-based and blind

rows.title: Auth bypass — HTTP verb confusion / override
rows.objective: Swap GET↔POST on auth endpoints; also test X-HTTP-Method-Override / X-Method-Override for auth-check inconsistencies or unintended verb routing to privileged actions

rows.title: Rate limit & lockout misconfiguration
rows.objective: Verify lockout triggers, check X-Forwarded-For bypass of rate limit

rows.title: MFA / OTP bypass
rows.objective: Response manipulation (change 403→200), code brute force, reuse of used OTP

rows.title: Account enumeration via timing/response
rows.objective: Compare server response time and body for valid vs invalid usernames

rows.title: Race condition on account creation
rows.objective: Concurrent signup requests with same email — duplicate account or credit bonus

rows.title: Email parameter manipulation
rows.objective: Add second email via %20, comma, CC param — attacker receives verification link

rows.title: Referral / invite code abuse
rows.objective: Reuse expired codes, self-referral, negative credit manipulation

rows.title: Token predictability & reuse
rows.objective: Check entropy of reset tokens, test reuse after use, test expiry enforcement

rows.title: Race condition on token consumption
rows.objective: Send concurrent reset requests — can two sessions use the same token?

rows.title: Host header injection in reset link
rows.objective: Inject attacker host in Host header — reset link points to attacker domain

rows.title: Change without old password verification
rows.objective: CSRF or direct API call to change password without providing current password

rows.title: Cross-user password change (IDOR)
rows.objective: Manipulate user_id or account param to change another user's password

rows.title: Unauthorized profile read (IDOR)
rows.objective: Access other users' profile data by manipulating ID in request

rows.title: Unauthorized profile modification
rows.objective: Modify another user's profile fields via IDOR on update endpoint

rows.title: Stored XSS in profile fields
rows.objective: Inject XSS in display name, bio, address — fires when admin or other user views profile

rows.title: Session alive after logout
rows.objective: Replay captured session token after logout — server must invalidate server-side

rows.title: Injection in session-related headers
rows.objective: X-Forwarded-For, User-Agent, Referer — injected into logs or DB queries

rows.title: LFI via language parameter
rows.objective: lang=../../../../etc/passwd — test path traversal in locale/language params

rows.title: Injection in locale setting
rows.objective: Inject special chars in language/timezone params — backend processing

rows.title: OAuth 2.0 / OIDC deep testing
rows.objective: redirect_uri bypass, PKCE downgrade, state CSRF, scope upgrade, authorization code injection, dynamic client registration SSRF (jwks_uri, logo_uri)

rows.title: Unauthorized user creation/deletion
rows.objective: Create or delete users under another vendor's account via BFLA

rows.title: Privilege escalation in user creation
rows.objective: Create a user with higher role than your own by tampering role param

rows.title: Cross-tenant transaction access
rows.objective: Access or refund transactions belonging to another vendor/user via IDOR

rows.title: Race condition on refund
rows.objective: Concurrent refund requests — trigger double refund via timing window

rows.title: Negative / zero value in payment
rows.objective: Submit negative amount — does it result in credit? Zero price bypass?

rows.title: Price parameter manipulation
rows.objective: Intercept and modify price/amount in request body before server processes

rows.title: Currency manipulation
rows.objective: Switch to weaker currency, manipulate currency code — pricing arbitrage

rows.title: Payment step bypass
rows.objective: Skip payment confirmation step by directly calling post-payment endpoint

rows.title: Replay / duplicate payment
rows.objective: Replay payment confirmation request — does server check idempotency?

rows.title: Injection in payment reference fields
rows.objective: SQLi/XSS in payment note, reference, description fields

rows.title: Injection in QR/PDF generation
rows.objective: SSTI or command injection via user-controlled data rendered into QR/PDF

rows.title: QR payment bypass from mini-app
rows.objective: Manipulate KHQR payload amount or recipient — bypass payment validation

rows.title: Coupon stacking race condition
rows.objective: Apply same coupon concurrently from multiple tabs/requests

rows.title: Unauthorized coupon code access
rows.objective: Access coupon list or codes belonging to another vendor via IDOR

rows.title: Coupon price manipulation
rows.objective: Intercept discount value in request — modify to 100% or negative

rows.title: Web shell upload bypass
rows.objective: MIME type swap, double extension (.php.jpg), null byte, content-type bypass

rows.title: XSS in uploaded filename
rows.objective: Filename like .jpg rendered in UI

rows.title: Command execution in filename
rows.objective: Shell metacharacters in filename processed server-side (e.g., image processing)

rows.title: HTML injection in email via filename
rows.objective: HTML in filename ends up in email notification — phishing vector

rows.title: XSS via SVG upload
rows.objective: SVG files can contain embedded JS — if rendered in browser context

rows.title: PDF content XSS / SSRF
rows.objective: SSRF or XSS embedded in uploaded PDF processed server-side

rows.title: Client-side bypass via response manip
rows.objective: Server returns allow/deny in response body — flip to bypass client-side file type check

rows.title: Path traversal in download endpoint
rows.objective: Manipulate file path param — ../../ to read arbitrary files

rows.title: IDOR in document retrieval
rows.objective: Change document_id or file_id to access other users' documents

rows.title: SQLi / NoSQLi in search query
rows.objective: Test search endpoint for injection — error-based, blind, time-based

rows.title: SSTI in search / template rendering
rows.objective: Test {{7*7}} and similar payloads if search term is rendered in template context

rows.title: GraphQL — introspection & enumeration
rows.objective: Enable introspection to dump schema, find hidden mutations/queries

rows.title: Reflected XSS in search results
rows.objective: Search term echoed unescaped in results page

rows.title: GraphQL — query depth / batching DoS
rows.objective: Deeply nested queries, alias-based brute force, batch mutation abuse

rows.title: Information disclosure via search error
rows.objective: Verbose error on invalid search — DB table names, stack trace

rows.title: GraphQL — IDOR via nested queries
rows.objective: Access related objects through nested query chains bypassing direct auth checks

rows.title: WebSocket — auth bypass & injection
rows.objective: Connect without valid session, inject payloads, cross-site WebSocket hijacking (CSWSH)

rows.title: HTML injection in email templates
rows.objective: User-controlled content in email — inject HTML to create phishing template

rows.title: Email header injection
rows.objective: Inject CRLF in To/From/Subject fields to add BCC, redirect emails

rows.title: CSV/Excel export injection
rows.objective: Inject formula payloads (=CMD|..., @SUM) into exported CSV/Excel via user-controlled fields — CSV injection / formula injection if opened in spreadsheet app

rows.title: Server-side injection in PDF/report generation
rows.objective: User-controlled data rendered into PDF/HTML report — SSTI, SSRF, or HTML injection via headless Chrome or wkhtmltopdf

rows.title: Open redirect in OAuth / OIDC redirect flows
rows.objective: Abuse redirect_uri, post_logout_redirect_uri, or relay/state-driven redirect flows to leak tokens, bypass allowlists, or chain phishing through a trusted OAuth / OIDC entrypoint.

rows.title: IDOR in report/export download
rows.objective: Manipulate report_id or export_id in download endpoint to access other users' exported data

rows.title: XML/CSV injection in file import
rows.objective: Upload crafted XML (XXE), CSV (formula injection), or XLSX (macro) via import endpoint — test server-side parsing

rows.title: Business logic bypass via bulk import
rows.objective: Import bulk data that bypasses per-item validation — negative values, duplicate IDs, privilege escalation via role field in CSV

rows.title: SSRF via import URL / remote fetch
rows.objective: Import feature that accepts a URL to fetch — redirect to internal services (169.254.169.254, localhost)

rows.title: Invite token reuse across tenants
rows.objective: Reuse or swap invite tokens between orgs, roles, or expired states to join the wrong tenant

rows.title: Privilege escalation through invite role tampering
rows.objective: Modify role, team, or org_id fields during invite acceptance to gain elevated membership

rows.title: Magic-link replay or cross-device reuse
rows.objective: Reuse consumed or stale magic links across browsers/devices to confirm one-time enforcement

rows.title: SSO state/relay parameter tampering
rows.objective: Alter relayState, returnTo, tenant, or state to pivot accounts, tenants, or post-login redirects

rows.title: Stored XSS through rich-text editor payloads
rows.objective: Inject HTML/Markdown/mention payloads that survive sanitization and execute in other user contexts

rows.title: Attachment/embed SSRF in comment previews
rows.objective: Abuse image, unfurl, or embed fetchers in comments to force server-side requests to internal hosts

rows.title: Plan downgrade without entitlement loss
rows.objective: Downgrade or cancel a plan and verify premium features, limits, and seat counts are revoked immediately

rows.title: Webhook/order state tampering on billing flow
rows.objective: Replay or alter subscription/payment status callbacks to activate service without a settled payment

rows.title: CSV formula injection in exported data
rows.objective: Place spreadsheet formulas in exported fields and verify dangerous formulas are neutralized on download

rows.title: Template injection in generated report exports
rows.objective: Inject report parameters or record fields into PDF/HTML export templates to trigger SSTI or SSRF

rows.title: Malicious file import parser abuse
rows.objective: Import crafted CSV/XLSX/XML payloads to test XXE, formula execution, parser crashes, or deserialization issues

rows.title: Cross-tenant import mapping abuse
rows.objective: Modify import field mappings or object identifiers so imported records overwrite another tenant’s data

rows.title: XSS via HTML file upload
rows.objective: Upload .html/.htm files (or spoofed content-types) — if served inline or same-origin, attacker JavaScript executes when victim/admin opens the file

rows.title: APK acquisition & integrity check
rows.objective: adb pull or APKPure — verify package signature, check for split APKs, use APKEditor to merge

rows.title: SSL pinning bypass — Objection / Frida
rows.objective: objection: android sslpinning disable; Frida: akabe1/frida-multiple-unpinning; Reflutter for Flutter apps

rows.title: Root detection bypass
rows.objective: Magisk allowlist, Magisk Alpha, Frida hook targeting root detection logic

rows.title: AndroidManifest.xml review
rows.objective: MobSF / manual Jadx — debuggable=true, allowBackup=true, usesCleartextTraffic=true, exported components without permission, over-declared permissions.

rows.title: Android component exposure review
rows.objective: Review AndroidManifest.xml and runtime registrations for exported activities, services, receivers, providers, intent filters, deep-link handlers, FileProvider paths, and unsafe component exposure. Test direct invocation, provider leakage, receiver abuse, intent redirection, and fragment injection inside this parent component review.

rows.title: Hardcoded secrets in source
rows.objective: Jadx decompile — search for API keys, tokens, DB credentials, internal URLs in strings.xml and code

rows.title: Flutter reverse engineering (Blutter)
rows.objective: blutter.py on arm64-v8a/libapp.so — extract Dart snapshot, generate Frida hook scripts from function offsets

rows.title: React Native bundle extraction
rows.objective: adb pull then: npx react-native-decompiler or strings — extract index.android.bundle; search for API keys, endpoints, secrets, internal URLs in plain JS source.

rows.title: Deep link and app link enumeration
rows.objective: Enumerate registered scheme, intent-filter, and app-link handlers with dumpsys/Jadx. Keep exploitation payloads in the Deep Links feature rows.

rows.title: Sensitive data in SharedPreferences
rows.objective: adb shell "run-as <pkg> cat /data/data/<pkg>/shared_prefs/*.xml" — tokens, passwords, PII in plaintext XML. Flagged: any key containing token/auth/pass/secret.

rows.title: Sensitive data in SQLite databases
rows.objective: adb shell "run-as <pkg> ls /data/data/<pkg>/databases/" then sqlite3 — dump all tables, check for tokens, credentials, PII stored unencrypted.

rows.title: External storage data leakage
rows.objective: adb shell "ls -la /sdcard/Android/data/<pkg>/" — world-readable files. Check for exports, caches, logs with sensitive data. Any other app can read /sdcard/.

rows.title: Logcat data leakage
rows.objective: adb logcat — check for credentials, tokens, PII logged during app operation

rows.title: Sensitive data in backups
rows.objective: adb backup -apk -shared <pkg> — check if backup is allowed and what data is exposed

rows.title: Memory dump for sensitive data
rows.objective: Fridump: frida -U -f <pkg> --no-pause -l fridump.py -- -s. Grep dump for token=, Bearer, password=, private_key. Also: adb shell "cat /proc/<pid>/maps" for memory regions.

rows.title: Cleartext traffic configuration review
rows.objective: Review AndroidManifest.xml, network security config, and static endpoint strings for cleartext HTTP allowance or plaintext service URLs.

rows.title: Clipboard data leakage
rows.objective: After login, trigger copy of sensitive data (password, token). adb shell "service call clipboard 2" or malicious app to read ClipboardManager. FLAG_SECURE does not protect clipboard.

rows.title: Debug mode enabled in release build
rows.objective: android:debuggable=true in manifest of release APK — enables ADB debugging on non-rooted device

rows.title: Root/jailbreak detection strength
rows.objective: Test detection with Magisk Hide, Zygisk/Shamiko — how robust is detection?

rows.title: APK repackaging & re-signing
rows.objective: Modify smali (e.g., flip SSL pin check), repack with Apktool, sign with test key, install

rows.title: Frida / instrumentation detection
rows.objective: App detects Frida gadget or ptrace — test bypass via Frida anti-detection scripts

rows.title: Sensitive data on lock screen / notifications
rows.objective: Trigger sensitive notification (OTP, balance, message). Lock device. Check if notification previews sensitive content on lock screen. NotificationCompat.VISIBILITY_SECRET should hide content.

rows.title: Screenshot prevention
rows.objective: Navigate to sensitive screen (balance, auth). Press Home. Check recent apps thumbnail — sensitive screen visible = FLAG_SECURE missing. Frida: hook getWindow().setFlags to verify.

rows.title: Overpermissioned third-party SDKs
rows.objective: MobSF — SDK inventory from decompiled APK. Burp — intercept traffic to third-party SDKs. Check: is IMEI/contact/location sent to analytics? Cross-ref declared permissions vs app functionality.

rows.title: Background data leakage
rows.objective: Background the app on a sensitive screen. Check recent apps for snapshot leakage. Also: Frida hook onPause() — does app blank content? FLAG_SECURE must be set on all sensitive Activities.

rows.title: Tapjacking / overlay attack
rows.objective: Build PoC overlay app (TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY). Target: payment confirm, auth screen. Check filterTouchesWhenObscured=true in layout XML or setFilterTouchesWhenObscured() in code (Jadx).

rows.title: Third-party SDK data leakage
rows.objective: Decompile and identify SDKs (analytics, ads, crash reporting). Intercept traffic for PII sent to SDK endpoints (device ID, email, location). Review SDK permissions — ad SDKs requesting Camera/Contacts. Use MobSF for automated SDK inventory.

rows.title: Accessibility service abuse
rows.objective: Malicious app with AccessibilityService can read all on-screen text including passwords and OTPs. Check if app implements AccessibilityService detection. Also: does app content show in accessibility tree (getContentDescription leak)?

rows.title: BOLA on mobile API endpoints
rows.objective: Mobile API often uses different auth or lacks server-side checks — test IDOR on all object IDs

rows.title: BFLA — admin functions via mobile API
rows.objective: Call privileged API functions available only via mobile client but not enforced server-side

rows.title: Mass assignment on mobile endpoints
rows.objective: POST extra fields to mobile-specific endpoints — role, balance, is_verified

rows.title: Weak auth on mobile-specific endpoints
rows.objective: Mobile app uses API key or device ID instead of proper auth — test without credentials

rows.title: API security misconfiguration on mobile backend
rows.objective: Check mobile-used endpoints for exposed OpenAPI/Swagger docs, debug or staging endpoints, verbose errors, weak gateway policy, and default credentials/misconfig inherited from the shared API tier

rows.title: Biometric bypass via Frida
rows.objective: Frida: hook BiometricPrompt.AuthenticationCallback.onAuthenticationSucceeded — force call success. Objection: android hooking search classes BiometricPrompt. Also patch CryptoObject null check.

rows.title: Token storage security
rows.objective: adb shell "run-as <pkg> cat shared_prefs/*.xml" — token in SharedPreferences = insecure. Secure = Android Keystore (KeyStore.getInstance("AndroidKeyStore")). Check with Jadx for storage location.

rows.title: Session management — token reuse after logout
rows.objective: Log out, capture auth token beforehand via Burp. Replay token after logout — expect 401. Also test: reinstall app, replay old token. Frida: dump token from memory post-logout.

rows.title: Deep link parameter injection
rows.objective: adb shell am start -W -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d "scheme://path?param=../../../etc" <pkg> — test open redirect, path traversal, XSS if loaded in WebView.

rows.title: WebView security
rows.objective: Jadx — check WebView.addJavascriptInterface (pre-API17 RCE), setAllowFileAccess(true), setJavaScriptEnabled on non-trusted URL. Frida: hook loadUrl to observe loaded URLs.

rows.title: Firebase / cloud DB misconfiguration
rows.objective: Jadx: grep for firebaseio.com, .firebaseapp.com, google-services.json. curl https://<proj>.firebaseio.com/.json — if returns data = unauthenticated read. Test .write via PUT. Check Storage: gsutil ls gs://<bucket>.

rows.title: JWT / token expiry not enforced
rows.objective: Capture auth token. Wait past expiry window or manually decode JWT (jwt.io) and check exp claim. Replay expired token — server should return 401. Also test: modify exp to future value, re-sign with none algorithm.

rows.title: Biometric hook bypass
rows.objective: Frida hook on biometric callback — call success branch directly without real biometric

rows.title: Auth token extraction from memory
rows.objective: Fridump during authenticated session — search memory for JWT/Bearer tokens

rows.title: Login response manipulation
rows.objective: Intercept login response — change false→true, 401→200 in auth response fields

rows.title: Credential storage location
rows.objective: Confirm passwords/tokens use Android Keystore — not SharedPreferences or hardcoded

rows.title: Deep link → WebView open redirect
rows.objective: Craft deep link with attacker URL as param — does app load arbitrary URL in WebView?

rows.title: Deep link parameter injection
rows.objective: Inject SQLi, XSS, path traversal via deep link query params processed by app

rows.title: Deep link → token theft chain
rows.objective: Deep link triggers auth flow, attacker-controlled redirect_uri captures OAuth token

rows.title: Payment request interception & tampering
rows.objective: Intercept payment API request — modify amount, currency, recipient before server processes

rows.title: Race condition on mobile payment
rows.objective: Trigger payment confirmation concurrently from two devices/sessions

rows.title: QR code injection / malicious QR
rows.objective: Scan attacker-crafted QR — does app process embedded deep link or payload unsafely?

rows.title: Payment step bypass via API call
rows.objective: Skip payment UI flow — call post-payment API endpoint directly to confirm without paying

rows.title: JavaScript interface abuse
rows.objective: Identify addJavascriptInterface — call exposed Java methods from injected JS

rows.title: File:// access in WebView
rows.objective: WebView loads file:// URIs — read arbitrary app files or even /data/data/ via XSS

rows.title: Open redirect into WebView
rows.objective: Any open redirect that loads in WebView context — phishing or JS injection

rows.title: Path traversal in file operations
rows.objective: Filename parameter in file open/save — ../../data/data/<pkg>/databases/main.db

rows.title: Insecure file provider exposure
rows.objective: FileProvider with overly broad paths — other apps can access private app files via content://

rows.title: OTP brute force and replay
rows.objective: Abuse resend, reuse, or parallel verification of OTP codes to complete registration without owning the channel

rows.title: OTP channel swap via client tampering
rows.objective: Change phone, email, or country-code parameters after challenge issuance to bind a verified OTP to a new identity

rows.title: Conflicted offline record overwrite
rows.objective: Queue offline mutations, alter local IDs/timestamps, then sync to overwrite protected server-side records

rows.title: Sync queue tampering
rows.objective: Edit queued requests or sync metadata on disk to escalate actions when the app reconnects

rows.title: Weak hardware-backed key usage
rows.objective: Verify tokens and secrets fall back insecurely when keystore/secure enclave access fails or biometric state changes

rows.title: Recovered secrets after app reinstall or migration
rows.objective: Test whether secrets survive uninstall, device transfer, or app restore in ways that bypass re-authentication

rows.title: Remote config trust bypass
rows.objective: Intercept or tamper remote config responses to enable hidden environments, debug flags, or premium features

rows.title: Unsigned feature flag package acceptance
rows.objective: Force the app to consume stale, unsigned, or attacker-hosted config bundles without signature validation

rows.title: Bound device swap via local state tampering
rows.objective: Modify bound-device identifiers, attestation state, or registration tokens to move a session to another handset

rows.title: Bypass device change approval workflow
rows.objective: Trigger device reset or recovery flows and skip step-up verification needed for re-binding

rows.title: Sensitive data restored from cloud/device backup
rows.objective: Back up and restore app data to confirm tokens, PII, and session artifacts are excluded or re-wrapped securely

rows.title: Rollback to privileged restored state
rows.objective: Restore older app data after logout, device bind, or step-up changes to regain a previously trusted state

rows.title: GraphQL introspection on mobile backend
rows.objective: Probe mobile backend GraphQL endpoints for schema introspection, hidden types, and undocumented operations exposed to the app.

rows.title: GraphQL IDOR / mutation abuse on mobile API
rows.objective: Abuse nested queries and mutations used by the mobile app to read cross-user data, over-post fields, or modify objects outside the current tenant/session.

rows.title: Mobile WebSocket auth token replay
rows.objective: Intercept the mobile app WebSocket handshake and replay or downgrade bearer/session tokens to test unauthorized channel reuse across devices or accounts.

rows.title: Mobile WebSocket message / subscription tampering
rows.objective: Modify subscription IDs, event names, and message payloads in the mobile real-time channel to test unauthorized event injection and cross-user data leakage.

rows.title: OAuth redirect URI / deep link hijack
rows.objective: Abuse mobile redirect URIs, app links, or custom schemes in OAuth / OIDC callbacks to steal auth codes/tokens or force the flow into an attacker-controlled handler.

rows.title: PKCE verifier or auth code replay in mobile flow
rows.objective: Test whether intercepted OAuth auth codes, PKCE verifier material, or stale state parameters can be replayed or swapped across sessions/devices in the mobile flow.

rows.title: Password reset token reuse in mobile recovery flow
rows.objective: Intercept or recover reset tokens, OTPs, or deep-link parameters used by the mobile app and verify whether they can be replayed across devices or reused after successful reset.

rows.title: Reset link / app-link hijack in mobile recovery flow
rows.objective: Abuse custom scheme or app-link password reset callbacks to steal reset tokens, swap the target account, or complete recovery from an attacker-controlled handler.

rows.title: Malicious file import/share parser abuse
rows.objective: Feed attacker-controlled documents, archives, or shared files into the mobile app import flow and test for parser crashes, unsafe deserialization, or trust bypass in imported content.

rows.title: Exported mobile report / statement payload injection
rows.objective: Generate exported statements, CSVs, or documents from the mobile app and test whether attacker-controlled values survive into files as formulas, scripts, or unsafe active content.

rows.title: QR payload tampering before payment confirmation
rows.objective: Intercept mobile QR/KHQR payment flows and alter merchant IDs, amounts, references, or redirect parameters before the app confirms the scanned payment request.

rows.title: Malicious QR deep-link / app-routing abuse
rows.objective: Test whether mobile QR or KHQR scans can trigger unsafe deep links, unintended app routes, or hidden mini-app/payment entrypoints without adequate user confirmation.

rows.title: Mobile coupon code tampering
rows.objective: Intercept coupon or promo-code apply requests from the mobile app and modify code, discount value, currency, eligibility, or cart binding before server validation.

rows.title: Mobile promo entitlement replay
rows.objective: Replay or reuse consumed mobile promo grants, referral credits, or campaign rewards across accounts, devices, carts, or checkout sessions.

rows.title: Mobile subscription entitlement tampering
rows.objective: Modify mobile subscription plan, renewal state, entitlement flags, or local purchase cache values and verify that the backend rejects unauthorized access.

rows.title: Mobile billing receipt / callback replay
rows.objective: Replay, alter, or duplicate mobile billing receipts and subscription status callbacks to test server-side verification, idempotency, and account binding.

rows.title: Mobile file upload validation bypass
rows.objective: Upload attacker-controlled images, documents, archives, or renamed payloads from the mobile app and verify server-side MIME, extension, size, malware, and content validation.

rows.title: Mobile file download authorization bypass
rows.objective: Modify mobile download identifiers, content:// references, signed URLs, or cached file paths to retrieve another user's documents or server-generated files.

rows.title: Cross-account mobile import mapping abuse
rows.objective: Modify import mappings, owner IDs, tenant/account IDs, or object identifiers so imported records overwrite or attach to another user or tenant.

rows.title: Mobile export authorization and path handling
rows.objective: Tamper export IDs, report IDs, local destination paths, and cached export references to confirm exported documents cannot expose another user data or write to unsafe locations.

rows.title: Mobile active-content upload handling
rows.objective: Upload HTML, SVG, PDF, archive, and polyglot files from the mobile client and verify same-origin serving, active content, malware, size, and server-side validation controls.

rows.title: Mobile cached download and signed URL reuse
rows.objective: Replay cached file paths, signed URLs, content URIs, and download tokens across users/devices to verify authorization is enforced on every retrieval.

rows.title: Mobile payment replay and idempotency
rows.objective: Replay payment confirmation, callback, and receipt requests from the mobile app to verify duplicate settlement, refund, and recipient changes are rejected server-side.

rows.title: Mobile coupon stacking race condition
rows.objective: Apply promo/coupon codes concurrently across app sessions, carts, and devices to verify stacking, reuse, and campaign limits are enforced server-side.

rows.title: Mobile entitlement cache rollback
rows.objective: Modify or roll back cached subscription, purchase, and entitlement state on the device and verify backend checks prevent unauthorized feature access.

rows.title: Mobile OAuth state and tenant tampering
rows.objective: Alter state, nonce, relay, tenant, account, and return parameters in mobile OAuth/OIDC flows to verify callback binding and anti-CSRF controls.

rows.title: Mobile cross-site WebSocket handshake abuse
rows.objective: Test WebSocket handshakes for missing Origin validation, weak token binding, and unauthorized cross-account channel establishment from attacker-controlled contexts.

rows.title: Mobile GraphQL depth and batching abuse
rows.objective: Send deeply nested, aliased, and batched mobile GraphQL operations to test resource exhaustion, authorization drift, and hidden mutation exposure.

rows.title: Mobile QR replay and confirmation binding
rows.objective: Replay scanned QR/KHQR payloads and confirmation requests across devices/accounts to verify amount, merchant, session, and nonce binding.

rows.title: Architecture identification (2-tier / 3-tier)
rows.objective: CFF Explorer, Wireshark, netstat — determine if app speaks directly to DB or through app server

rows.title: Technology stack identification
rows.objective: Detect It Easy (DIE), CFF Explorer — language, framework, .NET version, packer

rows.title: Network communication mapping
rows.objective: Wireshark + netstat -ano + Resource Monitor — identify all outbound connections and protocols

rows.title: All entry point identification
rows.objective: Observe all input surfaces: forms, file imports, URL handlers, IPC endpoints, clipboard

rows.title: Auth mechanism analysis
rows.objective: Observe login flow — local vs server-side, token storage location, session handling

rows.title: Hardcoded credential search
rows.objective: Strings, Ghidra, dnSpy — search decompiled/disassembled code for passwords, API keys, connection strings

rows.title: Hidden UI element exposure
rows.objective: UISpy / WinSpy++ / Snoop (WPF) / Accessibility Insights — enumerate all controls including hidden/disabled. Enable via AutomationElement.SetValue or memory patch IsEnabled property. Look for admin-only menu items.

rows.title: Disabled functionality activation
rows.objective: x64dbg / dnSpy — set breakpoint on IsEnabled/Visible check, patch return value. For .NET: dnSpy edit-and-continue to flip condition. Memory patch button state. Target: greyed-out admin features.

rows.title: Injection via GUI input fields
rows.objective: All GUI text inputs: login, search, file path, filter fields. Payloads: SQLi (OR 1=1--), command injection (| calc.exe), format string (%n%n). Trace with Procmon to see if input reaches DB/shell.

rows.title: Sensitive data in app files
rows.objective: %APPDATA%\<app>, %LOCALAPPDATA%, %TEMP%, %ProgramData% — dir /s /b *.log *.txt *.xml *.ini *.config. Search: findstr /si "password token secret key" *.* in app directories.

rows.title: Config file sensitive data
rows.objective: app.config / Web.config / appsettings.json / *.ini / *.xml — grep for connectionString, password=, apiKey=, token=. Also check encrypted sections: aspnet_regiis -pdf to decrypt if machineKey known.

rows.title: DLL hijacking via application path
rows.objective: Procmon filter: Process Name = app.exe, Result = NAME NOT FOUND, Path ends with .dll — identify missing DLLs loaded from writable path. icacls on app install dir — user-writable = plant DLL.

rows.title: Sensitive data in registry
rows.objective: Regshot: snapshot before/after app login — compare HKCU/HKLM writes. Search: reg query HKCU /s /f "password" and /f "token". Also: Procmon filter RegSetValue with sensitive data.

rows.title: Writable registry keys for persistence
rows.objective: AccessChk: accesschk.exe -kwsu "Users" HKLM\SOFTWARE\<app> — writable by non-admin = persistence or config hijack. Also check HKCU\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run for user-writable paths.

rows.title: Proxy-aware traffic interception
rows.objective: Set system proxy to 127.0.0.1:8080. Burp Suite / Fiddler (best for .NET — hooks WinHTTP). Check if app respects WinINet proxy. Fiddler: Tools > WinConfig to force proxy-unaware apps.

rows.title: Proxy-unaware traffic interception
rows.objective: ProxyCap / Proxifier to redirect by process. Echo Mirage for Winsock hook. Wireshark for raw capture. Target non-HTTP binary protocols. Look for plaintext auth, unencrypted data in custom protocol.

rows.title: Non-HTTP traffic analysis
rows.objective: Analyze TCP/UDP custom protocols and non-HTTP socket traffic with Wireshark, Procmon network events, and API Monitor hooks. Keep named pipe/local socket authorization checks in the IPC feature.

rows.title: TLS configuration
rows.objective: testssl.sh — weak ciphers, TLS 1.0/1.1, self-signed cert acceptance on thick client

rows.title: API security from desktop context
rows.objective: Run OWASP API Top 10 against the desktop app's backend API endpoints, including BOLA, mass assignment, BFLA, and security misconfiguration such as exposed docs, debug endpoints, verbose errors, and weak gateway policy

rows.title: Cleartext protocol usage
rows.objective: Wireshark — app sending credentials or data over HTTP, FTP, Telnet unencrypted

rows.title: ASLR / DEP / SafeSEH / CFG check
rows.objective: CFF Explorer, winchecksec — verify modern binary mitigations enabled on all DLLs and EXE

rows.title: .NET decompilation & logic review
rows.objective: dnSpy, ILSpy — decompile .NET assembly; review auth checks, license logic, crypto use

rows.title: Java/JAR decompilation
rows.objective: Jadx, CFR — decompile Java thick client; JNDI injection, deserialization gadget chains

rows.title: .NET deserialization
rows.objective: ysoserial.net: ysoserial.exe -f BinaryFormatter -g TypeConfuseDelegate -c calc.exe. Look for remoting endpoints, BinaryFormatter.Deserialize calls (dnSpy). Also ViewState without MAC — use ysoserial.net -p ViewState.

rows.title: Sensitive data and credential extraction from process memory
rows.objective: Inspect process memory and dumps for credentials, bearer tokens, passwords, private keys, and sensitive runtime artifacts during authenticated workflows. Use Process Hacker/procdump/strings and debugger-assisted dumping where needed.

rows.title: Electron — contextIsolation / nodeIntegration
rows.objective: Extract app.asar: npx asar extract app.asar app-src. Check main process package.json: nodeIntegration:true + contextIsolation:false = XSS leads to RCE via require("child_process"). Also check webSecurity:false.

rows.title: Electron — preload script injection
rows.objective: Review preload.js — what is exposed via contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld(). Can renderer call fs, exec, shell via exposed API? Frida: hook ipcMain.on handlers for injection via IPC messages.

rows.title: Weak file/directory permissions on app install
rows.objective: icacls "C:\Program Files\<app>\*" — check for user-writable files or directories in app path. Users group write = DLL/binary plant for privilege escalation or persistence. Also check %APPDATA%\<app> for world-writable sensitive config.

rows.title: Sensitive data in application event logs
rows.objective: Event Viewer (eventvwr.msc) > Windows Logs > Application — filter by app name. Also: Get-EventLog -LogName Application -Source <app>. Look for credentials, tokens, SQL queries, stack traces with internal paths logged by the app itself.

rows.title: Temp file credential capture technique
rows.objective: Lock Temp folder (disable Delete permission) before running app — credentials written to temp persist for inspection

rows.title: Unquoted service path
rows.objective: sc qc <service> — look for BINARY_PATH_NAME with spaces and no quotes. wmic service get name,pathname — automated check. Plant binary at first unquoted segment (e.g. C:\Program Files\Evil.exe).

rows.title: AlwaysInstallElevated check
rows.objective: reg query HKCU\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer /v AlwaysInstallElevated && reg query HKLM\... — both must be 0x1. If set: msiexec /quiet /i malicious.msi installs as SYSTEM.

rows.title: Custom Action DLL hijack
rows.objective: Procmon during install: filter msiexec.exe + CreateFile + NAME NOT FOUND — DLL in writable path = hijack

rows.title: Credentials in MSI tables
rows.objective: MyMSIAnalyzer / strings — check Property, Registry, CustomAction tables for plaintext credentials

rows.title: MSI repair mode privilege escalation
rows.objective: GuiFinder — identify MSIs running GUI as SYSTEM; exploit explorer.exe escape to get SYSTEM shell

rows.title: MST transform backdoor (unsigned MSI)
rows.objective: If MSI unsigned: craft malicious .mst transform, execute: msiexec /i legit.msi TRANSFORMS=evil.mst

rows.title: Embedded WebView full web pentest
rows.objective: Embedded CEF/Edge/WebView2 — run full web pentest: XSS (does it reach native?), file:// access, navigation to attacker URL, postMessage abuse. DevTools: --remote-debugging-port if enabled.

rows.title: DPAPI credential storage
rows.objective: CryptUnprotectData called by same user context decrypts DPAPI blobs — Mimikatz: dpapi::blob or dpapi::cred. Find blob: dir /s %APPDATA%\*.dat. Check if app stores DPAPI-encrypted creds in registry or file.

rows.title: Named pipe / local socket auth
rows.objective: pipelist.exe to enumerate named pipes. AccessChk to check ACLs on each pipe. Connect via CreateFile to test for missing auth or command injection. Look for privilege escalation via unauthenticated local pipe.

rows.title: Update mechanism MITM
rows.objective: Intercept update check traffic (Burp/Fiddler). Does update URL use HTTPS? Is response signature verified? Test: return crafted update manifest pointing to malicious binary. Check: pinning on update channel, version downgrade accepted.

rows.title: Bypass local auth check
rows.objective: Memory patch (x64dbg) or binary patch — flip auth result check from jne to je; always-true patch

rows.title: Credential in transit — desktop to server
rows.objective: Intercept login via Burp/Fiddler — plaintext or weakly hashed credential in transit

rows.title: Offline mode bypasses server auth
rows.objective: Disconnect network — does app enter offline mode with full access? Are cached creds protected?

rows.title: Cached credential protection
rows.objective: Search disk + memory + registry for cached credentials used in offline mode — DPAPI protected?

rows.title: License check patch
rows.objective: dnSpy/x64dbg — locate license validation function, patch return value to always-valid

rows.title: Clock manipulation for trial reset
rows.objective: Advance system clock — does trial period reset or extend? Check registry for trial timestamp

rows.title: Trial state in registry / file
rows.objective: Regshot — find where trial state stored; delete or modify to reset trial period

rows.title: License server request tampering
rows.objective: Intercept license validation API — modify response to reflect valid license

rows.title: Named pipe impersonation
rows.objective: pipelist.exe + AccessChk — writable pipe without auth; impersonate token of connecting process

rows.title: Local socket without authentication
rows.objective: 127.0.0.1 service accessible by any local user without auth token — SSRF or command exec

rows.title: COM object abuse
rows.objective: OleView — find COM objects registered by app; call methods without proper auth

rows.title: Unsigned update package
rows.objective: Intercept update download — replace with modified binary; does app verify signature before exec?

rows.title: MITM on update channel
rows.objective: ARP spoof / DNS poison update server — serve malicious update over HTTP or invalid cert

rows.title: Path traversal in update extraction
rows.objective: Zip slip — update archive extracts files to arbitrary paths outside update directory

rows.title: XSS → RCE via Electron shell.openExternal
rows.objective: XSS in rendered content calls shell.openExternal with attacker URL — executes OS commands

rows.title: contextBridge API abuse
rows.objective: Enumerate exposed contextBridge APIs — call privileged Node.js/native functions from renderer

rows.title: Full web pentest on embedded WebView
rows.objective: Apply web baseline (injection, auth, SSRF, XSS) to URLs rendered inside app WebView/CEF

rows.title: Import file path traversal
rows.objective: File import feature — craft filename with ../../ to write/read outside intended directory

rows.title: Malicious file parsing (RCE)
rows.objective: Import specially crafted document/image — trigger parsing vulnerability (e.g., image library CVE)

rows.title: Payment API request tampering
rows.objective: Intercept payment request — modify amount, recipient, currency before server processes

rows.title: Race condition on desktop payment
rows.objective: Concurrent payment triggers — submit same payment twice simultaneously

rows.title: Repair mode arbitrary file overwrite
rows.objective: Abuse repair/self-heal paths to plant files, replace DLLs, or write into protected locations

rows.title: Custom installer property injection
rows.objective: Pass crafted MSI/MSIX/public properties to alter install paths, service accounts, or post-install actions

rows.title: Custom URI handler command injection
rows.objective: Invoke registered scheme handlers with crafted URLs to break quoting and execute arbitrary commands

rows.title: Unauthorized privileged action via URI scheme
rows.objective: Trigger sensitive in-app actions through protocol handlers without existing session or CSRF-style confirmation

rows.title: Unsigned plugin loading
rows.objective: Drop or replace extension modules and verify signature, origin, and allowlist enforcement before loading

rows.title: Plugin sandbox escape through host API abuse
rows.objective: Use exposed host callbacks or IPC bridges from a plugin to access filesystem, exec, or privileged app services

rows.title: Sensitive data exposure in local database
rows.objective: Inspect SQLite/LevelDB/cache stores for tokens, credentials, report data, or decrypted secrets at rest

rows.title: Tampered local cache reaccepted by app
rows.objective: Modify cached entitlements, roles, or offline records and verify integrity checks occur before reuse

rows.title: Low-privilege control of privileged service channel
rows.objective: Abuse named pipes, RPC, localhost APIs, or job queues to make a service execute higher-privilege actions

rows.title: Formula/script payload in exported documents
rows.objective: Inject spreadsheet formulas, HTML, or active content into exported files consumed by internal users

rows.title: Export path traversal or arbitrary write
rows.objective: Manipulate save/export paths, templates, or filenames to write outside approved directories

rows.title: Update channel configuration tampering
rows.objective: Modify feed URLs, channels, or pinned cert settings to redirect the app to attacker-controlled updates

rows.title: Rollback to vulnerable signed version
rows.objective: Force downgrade to an older signed package and verify version pinning / anti-rollback protections

rows.title: GraphQL introspection exposed to desktop client backend
rows.objective: Identify GraphQL endpoints used by the desktop client and test schema introspection, hidden operations, and undocumented resolvers reachable from the app.

rows.title: GraphQL mutation / IDOR abuse via desktop operations
rows.objective: Replay and tamper with GraphQL queries or mutations issued by the desktop app to test cross-user object access, privilege drift, and excessive field updates.

rows.title: Desktop WebSocket auth/session reuse
rows.objective: Capture the desktop app WebSocket handshake and test whether session tokens, cookies, or bearer headers can be replayed to open unauthorized real-time channels.

rows.title: Desktop WebSocket event injection / subscription tampering
rows.objective: Modify event subscriptions, channel identifiers, and message bodies in the desktop client WebSocket traffic to test unauthorized event injection and cross-tenant leaks.

rows.title: Loopback redirect interception in desktop OAuth flow
rows.objective: Abuse loopback redirect listeners, localhost callback ports, or weak listener binding in desktop OAuth / OIDC flows to steal auth codes or tokens.

rows.title: Custom URI scheme token theft in desktop callback flow
rows.objective: Register or abuse custom URI handlers used for desktop OAuth / OIDC callbacks to capture tokens, swap state, or force the client into attacker-controlled redirects.

rows.title: Imported desktop document/parser abuse
rows.objective: Feed attacker-controlled spreadsheets, PDFs, or data files into the desktop import/open flow and verify whether parser trust, macro handling, or file-type validation can be bypassed.

rows.title: Desktop QR/KHQR payload tampering before render or print
rows.objective: Alter QR/KHQR payload fields generated or displayed by the desktop app and verify whether merchant identifiers, amounts, or references can be swapped without integrity checks.

rows.title: Scanned QR deep-link / protocol abuse in desktop client
rows.objective: Test whether QR/KHQR scanning or imported QR payloads can invoke unsafe protocol handlers, hidden desktop routes, or privileged actions without explicit trust boundaries.

rows.title: Desktop coupon code tampering
rows.objective: Intercept coupon or promotion apply requests from the desktop client and alter discount values, code ownership, campaign eligibility, or cart/session binding.

rows.title: Desktop billing entitlement tampering
rows.objective: Modify plan, renewal, paid status, or entitlement values in desktop API traffic and local state to verify backend authorization and license enforcement.

rows.title: Desktop subscription status replay
rows.objective: Replay or duplicate subscription activation, renewal, cancellation, or webhook-derived status messages and verify server-side idempotency and account binding.

rows.title: Desktop file upload validation bypass
rows.objective: Upload attacker-controlled desktop files, renamed payloads, oversized archives, or malformed documents and verify backend validation independent of client-side checks.

rows.title: Desktop file download authorization bypass
rows.objective: Tamper with desktop download identifiers, export paths, signed URLs, and cached document references to retrieve unauthorized files or overwrite unsafe locations.
